title: What OJT is and what to confirm with your school
summary: Start OJT preparation by checking your program's eligibility, required documents, placement approval and learning goals.
body:
OJT means on-the-job training: supervised work experience connected to a student's course or career preparation. ThinkMedia helps you prepare, find published opportunities and track an application. Finding a listing here does not mean your school has approved the placement or that a company will accept you.

Before applying, ask your instructor or OJT coordinator about your program's eligibility, required hours, endorsement or agreement forms, deadlines and placement approval process. Read each employer's listing for its own requirements, location and application instructions. Prepare a truthful résumé and any permitted documents; do not upload unnecessary sensitive information.

During OJT, agree on your supervisor, work expectations, feedback process and the records your school requires. If a requirement or policy is unclear, the coordinator and host organization are the authoritative sources for your situation. ThinkMedia Guidance cannot inspect their private rules or approve a placement. These boundaries follow the student preparation and opportunity workflow in the ThinkMedia requirements brief.

title: Find your way around ThinkMedia
summary: What students, instructors, companies and administrators can do, and where to find the main workspaces.
body:
ThinkMedia is a web workspace for OJT preparation, approved learning resources, published opportunities and application tracking. Sign in with the role assigned to your account. An administrator account is provisioned separately and cannot be chosen during registration.

Students can update their profile, browse published learning resources and opportunities, apply to an open listing once, track their own application status and read suggestions. Instructors can browse approved learning and public opportunities, but cannot open students' private applications. A company can edit its own profile and, after administrator verification, create and publish its own listings and review applications to them. Administrators verify companies, publish or moderate learning content, review reports and inspect audit history.

Use the navigation to open Learning, Opportunities, My applications or Suggestions as a student. Company tasks include Your listings and Applicants. Administrator tasks include Company verification, Learning content, Content reports and Audit history. A role only sees destinations it is allowed to use.

Guidance can explain these workflows but cannot inspect your private application, change a decision, verify a company or publish a listing. Check the actual workspace for live status. These instructions describe the implemented role boundaries in the ThinkMedia agent brief and API contracts.

title: Browse learning resources and OJT opportunities
summary: Find published guides and listings, use filters, and understand why a result may be missing.
body:
Open Learning to browse published resources. Search by topic or choose a topic filter, then open a resource for its full text. A resource may have a quiz; its score is based on the saved answer key. Students and instructors can use public learning resources, while draft or archived material stays out of the public library. Students can save or react to published resources. If you see no results, clear the search or filter and try another topic.

Open Opportunities to search published, available listings. Use the keyword, type, skill and location filters to narrow results. Open a listing to read the description, requirements and company details before applying. Draft and closed listings are not available for new student applications. A company can see its own drafts in Your listings; a verified company must explicitly publish a draft before students can find it.

Suggestions are a separate view. They explain why a public resource or eligible listing may fit your profile; they are not a placement, hiring or acceptance decision. Add accurate skills and interests to your student profile to improve the initial suggestions. Actual application decisions are shown in My applications. These instructions follow the implemented learning, marketplace and recommendation requirements in the ThinkMedia agent brief.

title: What Guidance can answer and what stays private
summary: Use cited preparation and platform help while keeping applications, documents and decisions in their authorized workspaces.
body:
Guidance answers preparation and platform questions using approved public guides and published learning resources. Open a cited source to inspect the text behind an answer. If the available material does not support the question, Guidance should say so rather than inventing a fact. A provider error does not block opportunities or applications.

Guidance is read-only. It does not receive private resumes, application records, profile details, session data or account credentials. It cannot submit an application, change a status, verify a company, publish a listing or decide whether a student is hired. Do not put unnecessary private details into a question.

For your actual application status, open My applications and read the status history. For a company's actual applicant queue, use Applicants while signed in as that verified company. For school-specific OJT hours, endorsement forms or placement approval, ask your instructor or coordinator; the platform does not define those local rules. These boundaries follow FR05-FR07 and FR10 of the ThinkMedia agent brief.
